components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        title:
          title: Title
          description: >-
            The optional honorific title of the pet owner (e.g. MR, MRS, MS, DR).
            When present it is combined with the lastName to form the owner's
            'salutation'. Stored and returned when supplied.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 10
          example: DR
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted for backward
            compatibility; when the structured 'addressLine1' is supplied it takes
            precedence. On a successful create the returned value is the composed,
            normalized address (the normalized addressLine1, with a single space and
            the normalized addressLine2 appended when addressLine2 is present).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the pet owner's structured postal address. Preferred
            over the flat 'address' when present; normalized on create (upper-cased,
            whitespace collapsed, common street-type abbreviations expanded).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the pet owner's structured postal address.
            When present it is normalized and appended to addressLine1 (separated by a
            single space) to form the composed 'address'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 4B'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80

            four digits and, for a city whose region is known (Sydney->NSW,
            Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), must fall within that region's postcode
            range (NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known

## Summary

I implemented the `riskFlag` feature for the owner-create/read flow in this Spring PetClinic app.

**What `riskFlag` means:** a derived-on-read boolean on an owner that is `true` when *any* of three conditions hold, else `false`:
1. **Possible duplicate** — the owner's stored `possibleDuplicate` flag is true (soundex(lastName)+postcode soft match).
2. **Disposable-adjacent email domain** — the email's domain is a *subdomain* of a known disposable-email domain (`mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, `guerrillamail.com`). Exact disposable domains are already hard-rejected with 400 at create time, so only subdomains survive to be flagged here.
3. **Over soft capacity** — the owner's stored `capacityWarning` flag is true (the city already held 40+ owners at create time, i.e. over the soft-capacity/warning threshold below the hard limit of 50).

**Changes made:**
- `src/main/resources/openapi.yml` — added the `riskFlag` boolean property (readOnly) to the Owner schema, which generates `OwnerDto.getRiskFlag()`. Documented the exact rule.
- `src/main/java/.../mapper/OwnerMapper.java` — added a `@Mapping` for `riskFlag` and two default methods (`deriveRiskFlag`, `isDisposableAdjacent`) plus the disposable-domain set, following the existing "derived on read" pattern (like `ownerSegment`).

I chose to derive `riskFlag` on read in the mapper because all three inputs are already available from the persisted owner (`possibleDuplicate`, `capacityWarning`, `email`) — no schema change or new persisted column was needed.

**Verification:** The new `Cp58Tests` (riskFlag false for a normal owner) passes, along with the related duplicate/capacity/email tests (`Cp10`, `Cp35`, `Cp38`), and the **full suite of all 58 test classes is green** (`BUILD SUCCESS`, 0 failures / 0 errors).

One judgment call worth flagging: the spec term "disposable-adjacent" wasn't defined anywhere in the repo, and no test exercises the *true* case for it. I interpreted it as "a subdomain of a blocklisted disposable domain" — the most natural reading given the existing exact-match blocklist — and documented that precisely in the OpenAPI description so the code and spec stay aligned.
